liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Caution: Do Not Step On Tracks** (1 review): Deadbase lists Caution as leading into Death Don't Have No Mercy [12]
- **Death Don't Have No Mercy** (1 review): Reviewer rates this take among the best the band ever did, in some ways better with the original lineup [8]
- **Viola Lee Blues** (1 review): Runs over 14 minutes and is judged excellent by the reviewer [10]
- **In the Midnight Hour** (1 review): Reviewer rates this take among the band's best, in some ways better with the original lineup [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **Stage Chaos/More Power Rap**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]
- **I'm A Hog For You Baby**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 5 archived performances [14]
- **Caution: Do Not Step On Tracks**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]
- **Star Spangled Banner / closing remarks**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]
- **Ken Kesey interviewed by Frank Fey**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Ken Babbs and harmonica**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Take Two: Ken Kesey**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Bull**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- Earliest performances in the archive: King Bee, Death Don't Have No Mercy, In the Midnight Hour [14]

## The recordings

- **gd65-acid-tests.sbd.bershaw.5406.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 44 songs; 273 min; rated 4/5 by 25 [1]. Said about its sound: The Prankster music collage sequence sounds beautiful but is cut short, leaving the reviewer wondering how long it ran; Reviewer concedes the playing and recording quality are not the best [7][11]

## Around the show

- Garcia's interview covers his thoughts on the war and on other bands such as the Airplane and Buffalo Springfield [5]
- The Garcia interview on Disc 4 is called fascinating for his talk about society changing [10]
- Deadbase places this show at the Fillmore Auditorium in San Francisco [12]
- Uploader finds the first eight tracks tighter and better recorded than the 3/12 or 3/25 material, dating them May 1966 or later [1]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd65-acid-tests.sbd.bershaw.5406.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by TaW and Alan Bershaw; source: See Info File [1]. Also: Fillmore Acid Test tracks dated 1/8/66 come from the officially released Key-Z productions video, per etree info; Sound City Acid Test tracks dated 1/29/66 come from the commercial CD The Acid Tests Vol. 1 [1]
